issues.problem: The deck provides only an Extend (stretch) slide and has no support tier, pre-built remix, or paired scaffolding for struggling learners, leaving the R0 'differentiation' gap unaddressed.
issues.fix: Add a support strand (e.g. a step-by-step tutorial or pre-built starter project) and pair it with the existing Extend as optional stretch so all learners reach the core forever-heart outcome.

issues.problem: The Evaluate slide asks open reflective questions but gives no observable success criterion or demo/exit-ticket check, leaving the R0 'answer_key' gap unaddressed.
issues.fix: Embed a visible success criterion (e.g. 'you can see the heart beat repeatedly') and a 2-minute demo or oral exit-ticket so the running device is direct evidence of understanding.

issues.problem: The deck explains 'forever' as an infinite loop but never warns that placing the heart animation inside 'on start' runs it only once, a documented key misconception for this task.
issues.fix: Add a teacher note contrasting 'on start' (single run) with 'forever' (repeats in the background) so students pre-empt the static-heart mistake.

issues.problem: Evaluate's reflective prompts ('How good is the project?', 'How does it work?') are open-ended with no concrete anchor, against UDL guidance to shorten reflective Evaluate and use a brief show-and-tell against a visible criterion for young kids.
issues.fix: Replace or supplement abstract prompts with a short peer show-and-tell where each child points to the two heart icons and a pause, describing what the program does.

issues.problem: Slide 5 teacher notes model frame timing purely via the two pause blocks, but 'show icon' carries its own ~600ms default display interval that is never mentioned, so learners may misread total frame duration when tuning pauses.
issues.fix: Note that each 'show icon' holds its image for a default interval and the pause adds to it, so shortening/longering pauses changes the beat without removing the icon hold.

issues.problem: The Extend tasks are listed flatly and not framed as clearly bounded, optional stretch for early finishers, and no mixed-ability pairing or starter-code scaffold is suggested for learners who need support.
issues.fix: Label Extend as optional 'finished-early' stretch, set an explicit stopping point, and suggest 1-device-pairing or a shared starter project for slower groups.
